entries.core_move: Express a periodic continuous-time signal in complex-exponential Fourier series form as a sum of integer-harmonic terms $C_k$ $e^{jk\omega_0 t}$ with each coefficient weighting one harmonic.
Interpret each complex Fourier coefficient $C_k$ as the magnitude-and-phase weight assigned to the kth complex-exponential harmonic in a periodic signal.
Evaluate complex Fourier coefficients by integrating $x(t)$$e^{-jk\omega_0 t}$ over any one period and normalizing by the period to isolate the kth harmonic.
Compute the DC coefficient $C_0$ by setting $k=0 in the complex Fourier coefficient integral and interpreting the result as the periodic signal's average value$.

entries.lesson_title: Relationship Between Trigonometric and Complex Forms
entries.core_move: Convert between trigonometric and complex Fourier series forms by mapping the DC term and each sine-cosine harmonic pair to the corresponding positive- and negative-index complex coefficients.
Interpret positive and negative harmonics as paired complex exponentials whose coefficients combine to represent each nonzero harmonic of a periodic signal.
